hook: Bend a diamond thin enough and it makes electricity.
what_happened: University of Hong Kong researchers used edge exfoliation to create flexible polycrystalline diamond membranes that generate electricity when bent.
why_it_matters: It breaks a century-old assumption that diamond is non-piezoelectric, transforming it from a passive structural support into an active electrical material.
the_catch: The voltage comes from boundaries between tiny crystals, not from diamond's own structure — so it needs polycrystalline membranes, and no working device exists yet.
caption: Researchers have discovered that bending ultrathin diamond membranes can generate electricity, breaking a century-old scientific assumption.
alt_text: A five-slide carousel explaining how ultrathin diamond membranes can generate electricity when bent.
